verdict.justification: Both deliverables accurately navigate the workspace constraints, recognizing that the governing notice period is 21 days (from approved record-r2.txt) rather than the unapproved 84 days in proposal-r3.txt. However, Deliverable A provides a vastly superior and mathematically consistent operational strategy. Recognizing that LPI can ramp up capacity to 2,500 units/month against a monthly demand of 800 sets, A structures a Last-Time-Buy (LTB) bank of 4,200–5,400 sets built within an 84-day extension window, combined with an early 'mould-ahead' of plastic parts so the plastic tooling can be released on Day 28. This solves the core supply chain puzzle: how to get the tools to India for the 3–4 month local plastics re-development without starving LPI of plastic parts while electronics take 4–5 months to localize. In contrast, Deliverable B proposes asking a hostile supplier who wants out immediately to keep supplying 800 sets/month for 5.5 months until April 2027, and contains contradictory timeline dates (claiming plastics will be ready in 'late Jan to late Feb-2027' even though the tools aren't moved until LPI's bridge stock is secure and require 25 days transit plus 3–4 months re-development). Deliverable A also includes crisp exception and decision rules that make it a much stronger executive negotiation guide.
